tema: Critical reply to Sharpe and Greco rejecting the characterization of ME/CFS as 'illness without disease'.
diseno: Opinion/reply article in bioethics; no empirical data.
hallazgos: Argues that medical explanations change over time and that conditions once considered psychosomatic turned out to be physiological; points out that Sharpe and Greco omit that many experts consider ME/CFS biomedical and reject the research that underpins CBT and GET.
conclusion: Medical classifications are revisable; calls for more humility before categorically asserting that patients have an illness without disease.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the conclusions text is just a list of references (noise), so triangulation is limited to two sources.

tema: Describes the development of the DePaul PEM Questionnaire (DPEMQ) from patient input.
diseno: Instrument development with input from hundreds of patients and preliminary validation against physical functioning; exact size not stated.
hallazgos: Significant and predictable relationships were found between different domains of the questionnaire and physical functioning.
conclusion: The DPEMQ offers a comprehensive measure of PEM; a paediatric version and consensus on scoring thresholds to meet symptom criteria are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The conclusions (discussion) focus on limitations and practical use (the possibility of applying only sections 2-5) and include funding noise.

tema: Analyses the aetiological relationship between postural imbalance and orthostatic intolerance in ME patients.
diseno: Original study in ME patients with OI using neurological examination and active standing test; sample size not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: Imbalance was present in 32.5% of patients with OI, circulatory alteration in 47.5% and both in 17.5%; in 37.5% neither was detected.
conclusion: Imbalance, associated with dysfunction of postural reflexes, would be an important cause of OI and intolerance of sitting, more influential than orthostatic tachycardia, and a sign of advanced disease.
triangulacion: The abstract is the opening text of the article and only contextualizes OI; keywords and discussion agree on imbalance and OI. The discussion acknowledges as a limitation that the mechanism is not clarified.

tema: Explores the relationship between resting heart rate and stroke volume index in ME/CFS, with and without POTS, versus controls.
diseno: Retrospective study of a tilt test database: 474 ME/CFS patients (314 with normal response and 160 with POTS) and 56 healthy controls; supine Doppler for stroke volume index.
hallazgos: Resting stroke volume indices were similar and the three groups showed an inverse relationship with heart rate with a similar slope. 15% of patients with a normal response and 29% with POTS had a resting rate above the upper limit of the controls.
conclusion: Patients have a higher resting heart rate per unit of stroke volume, especially with POTS, although most are within normal limits; this may have clinical and therapeutic implications.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions are more concise and do not reflect that most patients have rates within normal limits.

tema: Evaluates sustained attention as a possible biomarker in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with 84 patients (66 women, 18 men; Fukuda and Carruthers criteria) and 22 controls; MoCA, Toulouse-Piéron test (GIAP index), fatigue visual analogue scale and modified Borg scale.
hallazgos: Most maintain normal cognitive function, but 70% showed low or very low attention scores with marked cognitive fatigue versus controls (p < 0.05); no differences by sex in GIAP, although women perceived greater effort.
conclusion: The sustained attention deficit and fatigability after the test are a sensitive and reliable indicator that allows clinical suspicion to be supported and patients referred to confirm or rule out the diagnosis.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on sustained attention and mental fatigue; the conclusions speak of a biomarker and mild cognitive impairment in a small group, with no sensitivity or specificity data in the abstract.

tema: Determines the involvement of persistent HHV-6A/B, HHV-7 and parvovirus B19 in the development and severity of ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with 200 ME/CFS patients and 150 healthy individuals; simple, nested and quantitative PCR, restriction analysis for HHV-6A/B and immunoassays of antibodies and cytokines.
hallazgos: Active infection or co-infection was observed in 45% of patients versus 8.7% of healthy individuals, with higher viral loads. Patients with active infection had higher levels of IL-6, TNF-α, IL-12 and IL-10, and TNF-α, IL-12 and IL-10 were higher in the severe course than in the moderate.
conclusion: Persistent active co-infection by HHV-6A/B, HHV-7 and B19V is important in the development of ME/CFS, influences its severity and its markers could be used as diagnostic biomarkers.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are somewhat more ambitious than the abstract in proposing the viral markers as diagnostic biomarkers, despite a cross-sectional design.

tema: Speculates that glymphatic dysfunction, with accumulation of toxins in the CNS, would explain some cases of CFS and that CSF shunting could be therapeutic.
diseno: Hypothesis article based on neuroimaging evidence and CSF drainage studies. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Neuroimaging reveals structural and functional brain abnormalities in CFS; some patients could benefit from CSF drainage, which could be related to improved glymphatic flow and clearance of interstitial fluid.
conclusion: CSF shunting could restore glymphatic transport in a subgroup, but confirmatory studies are needed and, because of its invasive nature, it would be reserved for very severe patients or those with intense headaches.
triangulacion: Keywords, opening text (with the journal header) and PDF conclusions are consistent; the conclusions add caution about the invasive nature of lumboperitoneal shunting.

tema: Reviews the search for a blood diagnostic biomarker for ME/CFS, from biochemistry to electrophysiology.
diseno: Narrative review of studies on biochemical and electrophysiological properties of blood cells: Raman spectroscopy, electrical impedance with a nanoelectronic assay, metabolomics, mitochondrial dysfunction, cytokines and ion channels.
hallazgos: Several techniques separate patients from controls with high sensitivity and specificity, such as Raman spectroscopy of PBMC (91% accuracy) and impedance under osmotic stress. Cytokine profiles are poorly reproducible, the commercial ATP profile test has not been replicated and the dysfunction of TRP channels and acetylcholine receptors has not been evaluated as a biomarker.
conclusion: Various biochemical and electrophysiological properties are promising as quantitative blood biomarkers, but their specificity against other diseases and their practical feasibility remain to be evaluated.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on blood biomarkers, impedance, metabolomics and mitochondria; the PDF conclusions add the value of social validation of the diagnosis and specific criticisms of cytokines and the ATP test.

tema: Analyses the presence of active HHV-6 transcripts in post-mortem tissues of ME/CFS patients versus controls.
diseno: Study in a small cohort of post-mortem biopsies from ME/CFS patients and matched controls, using fluorescent in situ hybridization with a probe against the viral microRNA miR-aU14; exact size not stated.
hallazgos: Abundant HHV-6 viral miRNA was detected in several brain regions and neuronal tissues, including the spinal cord, only in ME/CFS patients and not in controls.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence of active tissue infection by HHV-6 and EBV in ME/CFS and justify reopening the debate on the role of herpesviruses.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the discussion text contains only ethics, contributions and funding. The conclusion mentions EBV, which is not described in the abstract's methods.

tema: Reviews the complexity of ME/CFS and long COVID: susceptibility, chronification of the immune response, neuroinflammation and subtypes.
diseno: Narrative review integrating the authors' own work (molecular responses to stress, exercise and vaccination). No sample stated.
hallazgos: Genetic and environmental factors determine susceptibility; individuals with the same clinical profile show unique molecular changes, and the same treatments can benefit, have no effect or harm. The transition from a transient to a chronic immune response and neuroinflammation are discussed.
conclusion: The interest and investment in long COVID offer opportunities to develop new therapies that would also benefit ME/CFS patients.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the discussion text only includes contributions, ethics and funding, so the conclusion comes from the abstract.

tema: Studies the role of tryptophan catabolites, inflammation and insulin resistance in the chronic fatigue and affective symptoms of long COVID.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 90 long COVID patients, 3-10 months after acute infection; tryptophan, catabolites (TRYCAT), HOMA2-IR, CRP and scales for physiosomatic symptoms, depression and anxiety; factor and regression analyses.
hallazgos: A severe endophenotype (22%) was identified with very low tryptophan and SpO2, and elevated kynurenine, KYN/TRY ratio and CRP. CRP, KYN/TRY and insulin resistance explained about 40% of the variance of the physio-affective phenome, predicted in turn by maximum temperature and SpO2 in the acute phase.
conclusion: The physio-affective phenome of long COVID is a manifestation of the acute and chronic inflammatory response, to which the decrease in tryptophan and the increase in kynurenine could contribute.
triangulacion: Full coherence among keywords, abstract and conclusions. CFS appears as a symptom domain (fibro-fatigue) within long COVID, not as a diagnosis.

tema: Evaluates whether daily supplementation with 500 mg of quercetin in phytosome form for 2 months relieves chronic fatigue.
diseno: Double-blind placebo-controlled trial; 78 subjects with chronic fatigue symptoms completed the study (40 supplement, 38 placebo; mean age 56 years). Primary outcome FIS-40; secondary PSQI, SPPB, steps with sensor, DXA and SF-12.
hallazgos: The difference in FIS-40 between groups was -10.583 points (p<0.001). There were significant improvements in PSQI (-2.040), number of steps (1443) and SPPB (0.248).
conclusion: Quercetin supplementation counteracts the symptoms of chronic fatigue, although the preliminary results require confirmation in large cohorts.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree. The conclusions (from the discussion, with noise from tables and funding) are more cautious than the abstract; two authors are employees of the manufacturer. The population is chronic fatigue of various aetiologies, not diagnosed ME/CFS.

tema: Scoping review to define brain fog in chronic musculoskeletal pain, its contributing factors and its functional correlates.
diseno: Scoping review according to the Joanna Briggs Institute and Levac et al. in Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Medline, with validation by patients and health professionals; number of studies not stated.
hallazgos: Four features of brain fog were identified (perceived variability, subjective cognitive dysfunction, participation limitations and functional changes) and a model with neuroanatomical/neurophysiological, mental health/emotional and environmental/lifestyle contributors.
conclusion: The inconsistency of the research prevents understanding of the phenomenon and may limit optimal care; specific measures and qualitative research are called for.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on brain fog, chronic pain and function; the focus is musculoskeletal pain, not ME/CFS.

tema: Report of the 2nd international congress of the Charité Fatigue Center (Berlin, 2023) on pathomechanisms, diagnosis and treatment of ME/CFS.
diseno: Congress report summarizing the presentations of more than 100 in-person researchers and more than 700 online attendees.
hallazgos: Key topics were the role of the immune system, endothelial and autonomic nervous system dysfunction, viral reactivation, new diagnostic measures and therapeutic approaches and clinical trials.
conclusion: Despite the greater attention given to COVID-19, ME/CFS remains very little researched and adequately funded research is needed to find diagnostic markers and targeted therapies.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions agree; the PDF places more emphasis on translating findings into therapeutic strategies, without providing specific results.

tema: Classifies ME/CFS patients using unsupervised learning on the SF-36 and relates it to peak oxygen consumption on CPET.
diseno: Two datasets: 2347 SF-36 records to train a clustering model and 239 patients with CPET (92 with complete SF-36) classified by Weber; chi-square test.
hallazgos: The Weber classification was directly associated with the SF-36 cluster; the matrix of 36 raw responses gave more reliable results than that of subscales (p < 0.05).
conclusion: Low oxygen consumption on CPET can be considered a biomarker of ME/CFS; the SF-36 analysed in primary care could facilitate early referral to specialized units.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions add the application in primary care and the need for multicentre validation; the biomarker claim seems strong for a validation with 92 patients.

tema: Relates the trajectories of daily hassles and uplifts to CFS worsening at six months.
diseno: 6-month prospective study with 128 CFS patients; weekly CHUS scale in online diaries; global impression of change; linear mixed-effects models.
hallazgos: Employment status was lower in the non-improved groups. The intensity of non-social hassles increased in the group that worsened and decreased in the group that improved; in the group that worsened, the frequency of non-social uplifts fell.
conclusion: Worsening is associated with distinct trajectories of hassles and a deficit of uplifts, with possible implications for behavioural intervention.
triangulacion: High coherence; the PDF conclusions propose scheduling non-social uplifts as an alternative with less risk than graded activity interventions, a more applied nuance than the abstract.

tema: Analyses volumetric differences in hippocampal subfields in ME/CFS and their relationship to clinical measures.
diseno: MRI with estimation of hippocampal subfields in 25 patients (Fukuda only), 18 (ICC) and 25 healthy controls; group comparisons and clinical correlations.
hallazgos: Only the ICC group had larger volumes in the left subiculum head (p < 0.001), presubiculum head (p = 0.0020) and left fimbria (p = 0.004). Correlations with fatigue, sleep, pain and SF-36 were stronger in the ICC group.
conclusion: The involvement of the hippocampus in the cognitive and memory problems of the ICC group is confirmed, and subiculum volumes could be a diagnostic biomarker.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on the subfields (subiculum, presubiculum, fimbria); the conclusions (from the discussion, with a lot of administrative noise) reinforce the role of the ICC criteria, absent from the keywords.

tema: Evaluates by ultrasound the limb musculature in fibromyalgia and its relationship to fatigue, severity and quality of life.
diseno: Controlled cross-sectional study with 152 subjects (102 patients with recent or established fibromyalgia and 50 healthy controls); ultrasound of muscle thickness and cross-sectional area and fatigue and quality-of-life scales.
hallazgos: In both patient groups, the smaller quadriceps area correlated with greater fatigue and lower quality of life and energy; in established disease, also with social isolation, and the lower biceps thickness with fatigue.
conclusion: Muscle measurements and quality of life are reduced in fibromyalgia even at diagnosis, which should be considered in treatment and follow-up.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions (discussion) add a central autonomic dysfunction hypothesis and the limitation of lacking biopsies. It does not address ME/CFS.

tema: Reviews the evidence on whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) as an adjunct treatment in chronic diseases with inflammation, including ME/CFS.
diseno: Narrative review with searches in PubMed, EBSCO and Clinical Key.
hallazgos: WBC could be used as an adjunct in systemic inflammation (rheumatoid arthritis) and in some patients with obesity; more controversially, in mild cognitive impairment, anxiety, depression, multiple sclerosis and multisystem disorders such as ME/CFS.
conclusion: The quality of the studies is generally low; randomized controlled trials with adequate samples and long follow-up are needed, also in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and the conclusions reproduce the abstract; the keywords do not mention ME/CFS, which is a secondary and speculative aspect of the review.

tema: Examines whether ME/CFS severity is related to the degree of cerebral blood flow reduction during the tilt test.
diseno: Study in two parts: 110 patients with repeat test (71 for worsening and 39 stable) and combined analysis of two previous studies (n=219) with severity according to ICC 2011 criteria.
hallazgos: In patients who worsened, the CBF reduction went from 19% to 31%, whereas in the stable ones it remained at 24%. In the combined data, the reduction was 25%, 29% and 33% in mild, moderate and severe disease.
conclusion: Severity and CBF reduction are strongly associated; the authors suggest a causal relationship and propose CBF to confirm worsening, guide treatment and assess disability.
triangulacion: The three sources agree; the conclusions broaden to practical uses (clinical trials, disability) and the abstract suggests causality from associative data.

tema: Examines whether supplementation with yeast beta-glucan and multivitamins relieves fatigue, unrefreshing sleep, anxiety/depression and quality of life in ME/CFS.
diseno: 36-week single-centre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 65 ME/CFS patients: beta-glucan with vitamin D3, B6 and zinc (n=35) versus placebo (n=30).
hallazgos: Supplementation significantly improved cognitive fatigue (FIS-40) at 36 weeks compared with baseline (p=0.0338).
conclusion: Yeast beta-glucan could relieve cognitive fatigue in ME/CFS; more interventions are needed to validate the finding and study immunometabolic mechanisms.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The conclusions text is noise (ethics, funding, conflicts), which reveals funding and supply of the product by the company. The improvement is expressed relative to baseline, not clearly versus placebo.

tema: Describes cytokine signatures in women with CFS/ME versus controls and the effect of anakinra on circulating cytokines.
diseno: Case-control study nested in a trial with 50 patients assigned to anakinra or placebo for 4 weeks and 48 matched healthy controls; panel of 92 inflammatory markers by PEA, ELISA for TGF-β and IL-1Ra and LASSO regression (NCT02108210).
hallazgos: IL-12p40 and CSF-1 were significantly elevated in patients; a combination of 47 markers gave a predictive model with a corrected AUC of 0.73. After correction for multiple comparisons, anakinra did not modify cytokines except IL-1Ra; TGF-β did not differ.
conclusion: There is an increase in IL-12p40 and CSF-1 and a set of predictive biomarkers; anakinra did not affect circulating cytokines except IL-1Ra.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions add the importance of sample handling and of detailed description of methods to replicate results.

tema: Compares familial genetic risk profiles in fibromyalgia, irritable bowel syndrome and CFS versus rheumatoid arthritis and major depression.
diseno: Study of Swedish national registers with 5,829,186 individuals; familial genetic risk scores based on aggregated risk of first- to fifth-degree relatives, adjusted for cohabitation.
hallazgos: FM patients carry substantial genetic risk not only for FM but for pain syndromes and internalizing, autoimmune and sleep disorders; IBS and CFS also show broad profiles but with lower mean risks, whereas major depression and rheumatoid arthritis have more restricted profiles.
conclusion: Functional somatic disorders would arise from a distinctive pattern of genetic vulnerability to various psychiatric, autoimmune, pain, sleep and functional somatic disorders, more marked in FM than in IBS and CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (taken from the abstract) are consistent; the main focus is FM and CFS appears as a secondary case with a less marked pattern, and the keywords frame CFS within functional somatic syndromes.

tema: Reviews the current evidence on clinical diagnosis and randomized controlled trials in ME/CFS and its similarities and differences with long COVID and post-COVID.
diseno: Narrative review in German. No sample stated.
hallazgos: According to the authors, after years of research no clear causal pathophysiological results or evidence-based therapies have been identified, and there are evident rates of psychiatric comorbidity.
conclusion: The authors maintain that a psychosomatic aetiology should be considered and that a stricter diagnostic classification would benefit research.
triangulacion: No conclusions are available; keywords (diagnosis, criteria, RCT) and abstract are consistent. Its psychosomatic approach contrasts with the biomedical orientation of most works on the topic.

tema: Doctoral thesis that develops a neuroinflammatory paradigm to explain ME/CFS and post-COVID-19 fatigue syndrome (PCFS).
diseno: Doctoral thesis (University of Otago, 2023) based on a literature review of neuroimaging (PET/MRI, MR spectroscopy) and CSF, with a model proposal. No sample stated.
hallazgos: The absence of brain nociceptors and the low sensitivity of neuroimaging would explain why chronic low-grade neuroinflammation has gone unnoticed; overactivation of microglia and astrocytes in the limbic system and hypothalamic dysfunction would alter the autonomic nervous system.
conclusion: If confirmed as neuroinflammatory diseases, ME/CFS and PCFS would be potentially reversible; the proposed model is offered as a framework for others to test.
triangulacion: There are no keywords. The opening text and the conclusions are consistent; the conclusions have a more speculative and hopeful tone (5-10 year horizon) than the abstract.
